name: manual_e6771a
claim: A script that runs 'git -C <other-repo>' against multiple repositories, when itself invoked as a git hook (or from within a hook's call chain), must clear git's own local-environment variables first -- 'unset' every name from 'git rev-parse --local-env-vars' (GIT_DIR, GIT_WORK_TREE, GIT_INDEX_FILE, etc.) before the first cross-repo git call. Hooks export these for their OWN repo context; left set, they silently rebind every subsequent '-C <other-repo>' call back to the invoking repo instead of the target.

decisions.notes: Found by another agent (Codex): the first linked-worktree scope fix (see lesson on git-common-dir) worked in isolated testing but failed when actually invoked as a real pre-push hook, because GIT_DIR was already exported in that process's environment and silently redirected every 'git -C <sibling>' call back to the pushing repo -- an independent sibling could then be skipped as if it were a match. Fixed in orama-system PR 313 (fix/guard-hook-git-env-20260814), synced to PT as commit ef80f9a5. Using git's own 'rev-parse --local-env-vars' introspection instead of hardcoding 'unset GIT_DIR' is the more robust form -- future-proof against git adding new local env vars.
